From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law
**Status:** Draft for internal discussion. The Seller's papers are the other side's draft and have been reviewed as untrusted material.

---

## Overview

The Seller's cover note says its package is "fair and balanced." Its own Disclosure Letter contradicts several of its positions.

- **Bluefen:** The Seller says the consent is "addressed," but the letter says no consent is included.
- **Riverlark:** The Seller says the release will follow Completion, but the letter says the facility is unpaid and there is no discharge.
- **Incident:** The Seller says it is "not expected to be material," but the letter says the scope and access are unknown and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Bonuses:** The Seller calls them "a matter for the Seller," yet they are a liability of the Company and are left out of the funds flow.

The Seller's protective drafting adds to this:

- limitations and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature";
- disclosure is general;
- there is a buyer-knowledge bar;
- fundamental warranties are folded into the general regime.

Together, these would leave the Buyer with very little recourse for exactly the risks the letter identifies. **Overall:** reject the "one regime fits all" architecture. Deal with the known issues through conditions, completion deliverables, price and funds-flow mechanics, and specific indemnities outside the general limits.

**Timing:** The disclosure is "as at 22 September 2026," which is more than six weeks old. Ask for a refreshed data room and an updated letter, and require the warranties to be repeated at Completion.

---

## Issue-by-Issue

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** A higher cap, opening at 40–50% (AUD 9.6–12m), with a likely landing of 30–35%. The cap should apply only to general warranties. Fundamental, title, tax and specific indemnity claims should be capped at 100% of price, or uncapped for fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. 20% is light given the known exposures (Bluefen is ~30% of revenue, plus IP and privacy risk). If W&I insurance is being considered, the cap could be negotiated around the policy instead.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000 (about 1% of price); only the excess over the basket is recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - De minimis of about AUD 10,000.
  - Basket of about AUD 120,000 (0.5%).
  - A **tipping** basket, so the full amount is recoverable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
  - Related or recurring claims aggregated for de minimis purposes.
  - None of these thresholds applying to fundamental, tax or specific indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. An excess-only basket of 250k plus a non-aggregating de minimis would screen out a large share of realistic claims. The aggregation point matters directly for the split Sandbar renewals (N-013).

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. Limitations apply to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - 24 months for general warranties, which covers at least two full audit cycles.
  - Tax: 7 years, or the relevant amendment period plus 6 months.
  - Fundamental and title: 7 years (beyond the 6-year NSW contract limitation period).
  - Specific indemnities: the longer of 3 years and 6 months after the underlying matter is finally resolved.
- **Recommendation:** Counter, and reverse the default. Short limits must not carry over to other categories automatically (see N-014).

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** Capacity, authority, title, no-encumbrance and share-capital warranties to:
  - be capped at 100% of price;
  - have a time limit of at least 7 years;
  - have no de minimis or basket;
  - not be qualified by disclosure or Buyer knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Under the Seller's draft, if title fails the Buyer could recover only AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m purchase. "Simplicity" is not a justification for that.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out so that no limitation, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance or knowledge provision applies to claims arising from fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller, its related parties, the Company's management or advisers. Statutory misleading-conduct claims (ACL s 18) should also be preserved to the extent they cannot be excluded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's wording and insert the carve-out. It is market-standard, and its absence is a red flag given how many matters the Seller's own papers understate.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Only specific disclosures in the letter, made fairly and with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its impact.
  - Delete general data-room and public-records disclosure. As a fallback, limit it to an agreed, indexed and USB-archived data room and named searches dated within 3 days before signing.
  - No disclosure against fundamental or tax warranties, or against specific indemnities.
  - Make clear that disclosure cannot reduce any indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the general disclosure. Combined with N-007, it would hollow out the warranties. Clause 1.4 ("no admission... of materiality") also needs to be read down so it cannot defeat indemnity claims.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Buyer should want:** Deletion, replaced by a pro-sandbagging clause. Buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, does not affect any claim, except to the extent a matter is *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter. Constructive and "discoverable" knowledge, and adviser knowledge, must not be imputed.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. In effect it converts diligence into a waiver, and "discoverable" knowledge makes the warranties close to illusory.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** "Addressed." Reasonable endeavours; treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure ¶2 confirms that no consent has been obtained and that the 11.3 conditions are unverified.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A **condition precedent** of unconditional written consent under cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably).
  - Evidence that all 11.3 conditions are satisfied, or that any remaining conditions are acceptable to the Buyer.
  - The condition to be waivable only by the Buyer.
  - A long-stop date with a Buyer termination right.
  - Seller obligation upgraded to "all reasonable endeavours," with the Buyer involved in communications with Bluefen.
  - Fallback: if the condition is waived, a price adjustment or escrow, and a specific indemnity for loss of the contract within 12–24 months that is linked to the change of control.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a Buyer-protective CP. About 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m) depends on this. Delivery of "a consent" with unmet conditions is not sufficient.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with the release to be "provided following Completion." Disclosure ¶3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge has been given.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Repayment **at** Completion out of the price, as Debt under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.
  - A completion deliverable package from Riverlark: a payoff letter with a per-diem figure, and an executed deed of release and discharge, including PPSR/ASIC releases and release of any security over the shares.
  - Direct payment to Riverlark in the funds flow.
  - A specific indemnity for any residual amounts or fees, including any break costs triggered by change of control (cl 8.1).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. Without it the Buyer would pay for an encumbered business. The change-control clause may also put the Company in default at Completion.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 in Completion bonuses (DD-005) is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. The letter is silent on on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The bonuses, plus employer superannuation, payroll tax, PAYG withholding and other on-costs, treated as **Transaction Expenses / Debt** that reduce the price.
  - Payment through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded from the price.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall and for any related tax or superannuation liabilities.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise and deduct. The liability sits with the Company, so the Buyer bears it in substance unless the funds flow addresses it. On-costs could add tens of thousands of dollars on top of the 420k.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate." Disclosure ¶4 confirms that under DD-004 cl 7.3 title to the SOW3 materials only transfers on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, with no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A **completion deliverable**: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees, ideally Seller-funded, plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment and waiver of claims from Ironquay.
  - Failing that, a specific indemnity covering *all* loss arising from the Company's failure to own the SOW3 Project Materials. This would include infringement claims, re-development and licensing costs, and loss of customer revenue that depends on those materials.
  - The indemnity to sit outside the cap, basket and disclosure, backed by an escrow or retention (for example AUD 500k–1m, sized after technical diligence on how dependent the business is on the materials).
- **Recommendation:** Reject "adequate." Paying AUD 180k does not solve the problem without an assignment, and the risk is about ownership of core IP rather than a debt.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." Disclosure ¶6 says:
  - about 1,240 records were sent to an unintended external address;
  - it is unknown whether anyone accessed the file;
  - the scope is unknown;
  - it is undetermined whether notification is required.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Before signing or Completion: the Seller to procure a completed eligible-data-breach assessment under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), the attempted retrieval and deletion attestation, forensic findings, and records of any notifications to the OAIC or affected individuals.
  - A specific warranty that the assessment and any notification obligations have been complied with.
  - A **specific indemnity** for all costs, regulatory penalties, claims, remediation and notification costs, outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, with an extended time limit.
  - A conduct-of-business covenant giving the Buyer visibility and consultation rights.
  - A retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus pre-Completion remediation. **Urgent point:** the incident pre-dates 22 September 2026. The 30-day assessment period under the NDB scheme has very likely expired, so the Company may already be non-compliant. The Seller's papers do not say whether the assessment was completed.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 in total) are "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure ¶8 admits they are related and should be "read together," and says nothing on whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Copies of all three renewals.
  - Confirmation of the approval route, and in particular whether the split avoided a board or conduct-of-business consent threshold.
  - Termination rights and costs.
  - Accounting treatment: any prepaid, committed or accrued amounts to be treated as Debt or adjusted through completion accounts.
  - A pre-Completion covenant that no further renewals are made without Buyer consent.
  - A specific warranty or indemnity for any non-arm's-length or non-ordinary-course commitments.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label. Splitting one commitment into three equal related contracts is a classic way to avoid thresholds. Aggregation under N-002 must capture this kind of split.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Limitations apply to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise." Fundamental warranties are folded into the general regime, and limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions are blanket.
- **Buyer should want:** Express, separately ringfenced regimes for each category:
  1. General warranties;
  2. Fundamental and title warranties;
  3. Tax warranties and the tax indemnity;
  4. Specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy incident, bonuses and on-costs, Riverlark, Sandbar, Bluefen fallback);
  5. Price, Debt and leakage adjustments;
  6. Fraud.

  General limitations should apply **only** to category 1 unless the agreement expressly says otherwise, which reverses the Seller's default. Funds-flow items (Riverlark, bonuses) are price mechanics, not warranty claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reverse the default. A drafting oversight under the Seller's formulation would cap every specific indemnity at the general warranty limits.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register (DD-012). Disclosure ¶10 concedes the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Independent verification: an ASIC company extract reconciled to the register, share certificates, the issue and transfer history with board approvals, a constitution check (pre-emption rights and transfer restrictions), and PPSR searches against the Seller and Company.
  - Confirmation that there is no Riverlark or other security over the shares.
  - Fundamental warranties (N-004) of full legal and beneficial title, free of Encumbrances.
  - Completion deliverables: executed share transfer forms, original certificates, board resolutions approving the transfer and updating the register, any pre-emption waivers, and security releases.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone. A company's internal register is not conclusive evidence of title, and a Riverlark share security would directly defeat a clean transfer.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considers tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, general disclosure).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:**
    - a standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes on a dollar-for-dollar basis;
    - no thresholds and no disclosure against it;
    - a time limit of 7 years or the amendment period plus 6 months;
    - a cap of 100% of price;
    - Buyer-controlled conduct provisions with Seller consultation;
    - express coverage of payroll tax, superannuation guarantee (including on the DD-005 bonuses) and any employment-status risk.
  - **IP:** Elevated IP warranties covering ownership, valid assignments from employees and contractors (including Ironquay), non-infringement, open-source compliance and data and privacy compliance. These should carry a higher cap (for example 50–100%) and a time limit of at least 3 years, with Ironquay and the incident handled by the specific indemnities above.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled." These have not been negotiated. The tax amendment periods and the identified IP and privacy issues mean the general regime is the wrong vehicle.

---

## Other points to raise (not in the list)
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** Obtain the clauses and confirm that notice only is required for the lease and that no consent is required on a share sale. Make giving the lease notice a Completion deliverable.
- **Repetition and bring-down:** Warranties should be repeated at Completion. Add a Buyer termination right for material breach or a Material Adverse Change between signing and Completion.
- **Leakage / conduct of business:** Restrict new contracts, renewals, bonuses and payments to related parties without Buyer consent.

## Suggested next steps
1. Issue an information request covering: the Bluefen 11.2/11.3 status, the Riverlark payoff figures and security list, Ironquay payment evidence, the incident file and NDB assessment, the Sandbar contracts and approvals, the DD-005 bonus terms and on-costs, the constitution and ASIC/PPSR searches, and a refreshed data room.
2. Commission Buyer-side forensic and privacy review of DD-006, and technical review of SOW3 dependency, so the retention can be sized.
3. Prepare a Buyer mark-up reflecting the above, led by the regime architecture (N-014), fraud (N-005), disclosure and knowledge (N-006/007) and CPs (N-008).

The figures above are suggested opening and landing positions for internal discussion, not fixed recommendations. The deal team should confirm risk appetite, W&I strategy and commercial priorities before the mark-up issues.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** "Addressed." Reasonable endeavours; treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure ¶2 confirms that no consent has been obtained and that the 11.3 conditions are unverified.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A **condition precedent** of unconditional written consent under cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably).
  - Evidence that all 11.3 conditions are satisfied, or that any remaining conditions are acceptable to the Buyer.
  - The condition to be waivable only by the Buyer.
  - A long-stop date with a Buyer termination right.
  - Seller obligation upgraded to "all reasonable endeavours," with the Buyer involved in communications with Bluefen.
  - Fallback: if the condition is waived, a price adjustment or escrow, and a specific indemnity for loss of the contract within 12–24 months that is linked to the change of control.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a Buyer-protective CP. About 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m) depends on this. Delivery of "a consent" with unmet conditions is not sufficient.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with the release to be "provided following Completion." Disclosure ¶3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge has been given.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Repayment **at** Completion out of the price, as Debt under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.
  - A completion deliverable package from Riverlark: a payoff letter with a per-diem figure, and an executed deed of release and discharge, including PPSR/ASIC releases and release of any security over the shares.
  - Direct payment to Riverlark in the funds flow.
  - A specific indemnity for any residual amounts or fees, including any break costs triggered by change of control (cl 8.1).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. Without it the Buyer would pay for an encumbered business. The change-control clause may also put the Company in default at Completion.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 in Completion bonuses (DD-005) is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. The letter is silent on on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The bonuses, plus employer superannuation, payroll tax, PAYG withholding and other on-costs, treated as **Transaction Expenses / Debt** that reduce the price.
  - Payment through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded from the price.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall and for any related tax or superannuation liabilities.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise and deduct. The liability sits with the Company, so the Buyer bears it in substance unless the funds flow addresses it. On-costs could add tens of thousands of dollars on top of the 420k.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate." Disclosure ¶4 confirms that under DD-004 cl 7.3 title to the SOW3 materials only transfers on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, with no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A **completion deliverable**: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees, ideally Seller-funded, plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment and waiver of claims from Ironquay.
  - Failing that, a specific indemnity covering *all* loss arising from the Company's failure to own the SOW3 Project Materials. This would include infringement claims, re-development and licensing costs, and loss of customer revenue that depends on those materials.
  - The indemnity to sit outside the cap, basket and disclosure, backed by an escrow or retention (for example AUD 500k–1m, sized after technical diligence on how dependent the business is on the materials).
- **Recommendation:** Reject "adequate." Paying AUD 180k does not solve the problem without an assignment, and the risk is about ownership of core IP rather than a debt.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." Disclosure ¶6 says:
  - about 1,240 records were sent to an unintended external address;
  - it is unknown whether anyone accessed the file;
  - the scope is unknown;
  - it is undetermined whether notification is required.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Before signing or Completion: the Seller to procure a completed eligible-data-breach assessment under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), the attempted retrieval and deletion attestation, forensic findings, and records of any notifications to the OAIC or affected individuals.
  - A specific warranty that the assessment and any notification obligations have been complied with.
  - A **specific indemnity** for all costs, regulatory penalties, claims, remediation and notification costs, outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, with an extended time limit.
  - A conduct-of-business covenant giving the Buyer visibility and consultation rights.
  - A retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus pre-Completion remediation. **Urgent point:** the incident pre-dates 22 September 2026. The 30-day assessment period under the NDB scheme has very likely expired, so the Company may already be non-compliant. The Seller's papers do not say whether the assessment was completed.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 in total) are "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure ¶8 admits they are related and should be "read together," and says nothing on whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Copies of all three renewals.
  - Confirmation of the approval route, and in particular whether the split avoided a board or conduct-of-business consent threshold.
  - Termination rights and costs.
  - Accounting treatment: any prepaid, committed or accrued amounts to be treated as Debt or adjusted through completion accounts.
  - A pre-Completion covenant that no further renewals are made without Buyer consent.
  - A specific warranty or indemnity for any non-arm's-length or non-ordinary-course commitments.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label. Splitting one commitment into three equal related contracts is a classic way to avoid thresholds. Aggregation under N-002 must capture this kind of split.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Limitations apply to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise." Fundamental warranties are folded into the general regime, and limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions are blanket.
- **Buyer should want:** Express, separately ringfenced regimes for each category:
  1. General warranties;
  2. Fundamental and title warranties;
  3. Tax warranties and the tax indemnity;
  4. Specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy incident, bonuses and on-costs, Riverlark, Sandbar, Bluefen fallback);
  5. Price, Debt and leakage adjustments;
  6. Fraud.

  General limitations should apply **only** to category 1 unless the agreement expressly says otherwise, which reverses the Seller's default. Funds-flow items (Riverlark, bonuses) are price mechanics, not warranty claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reverse the default. A drafting oversight under the Seller's formulation would cap every specific indemnity at the general warranty limits.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the share register (DD-012). Disclosure ¶10 concedes the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Independent verification: an ASIC company extract reconciled to the register, share certificates, the issue and transfer history with board approvals, a constitution check (pre-emption rights and transfer restrictions), and PPSR searches against the Seller and Company.
  - Confirmation that there is no Riverlark or other security over the shares.
  - Fundamental warranties (N-004) of full legal and beneficial title, free of Encumbrances.
  - Completion deliverables: executed share transfer forms, original certificates, board resolutions approving the transfer and updating the register, any pre-emption waivers, and security releases.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone. A company's internal register is not conclusive evidence of title, and a Riverlark share security would directly defeat a clean transfer.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considers tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, general disclosure).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:**
    - a standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes on a dollar-for-dollar basis;
    - no thresholds and no disclosure against it;
    - a time limit of 7 years or the amendment period plus 6 months;
    - a cap of 100% of price;
    - Buyer-controlled conduct provisions with Seller consultation;
    - express coverage of payroll tax, superannuation guarantee (including on the DD-005 bonuses) and any employment-status risk.
  - **IP:** Elevated IP warranties covering ownership, valid assignments from employees and contractors (including Ironquay), non-infringement, open-source compliance and data and privacy compliance. These should carry a higher cap (for example 50–100%) and a time limit of at least 3 years, with Ironquay and the incident handled by the specific indemnities above.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled." These have not been negotiated. The tax amendment periods and the identified IP and privacy issues mean the general regime is the wrong vehicle.

## Other points to raise (not in the list)
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** Obtain the clauses and confirm that notice only is required for the lease and that no consent is required on a share sale. Make giving the lease notice a Completion deliverable.
